title: Observed Request Handshake and Trace Resolver
creator: Jordan Kim
description:
Problem: We currently have several ad-hoc propagation shims across SDKs and edge proxies which lead to dropped trace linkage when requests cross internal and external boundaries (edge -> api-gateway -> runtime). This causes gaps in end-to-end latency and error attribution.

Goal: Implement an "observed request handshake" pattern and a central Trace Resolver component that: 1) provides a deterministic, low-overhead handshake between ingress proxies and internal services to reconcile partial carriers; 2) normalizes and enriches propagation headers (legacy and OpenTelemetry formats) into a canonical request envelope used by our runtime; 3) surfaces fidelity hints so downstream systems can choose sampling/aggregation strategies (e.g., preserve full spans for high-fidelity routes).

Scope: SDK middleware and server-side request interceptor implementations for Node, Go, and Python; an HTTP/GRPC ingress adapter for the edge-proxy (sidecar) to perform early reconciliation; a server-side Trace Resolver library used by the runtime to canonicalize carriers and emit consistent span attributes; accompanying schema for the canonical envelope.

Non-goals: Rewriting existing SDKs end-to-end (we will provide compatibility adapters and gradual opt-in), implementing new sampling algorithms beyond metadata propagation, or changing downstream storage/retention policies for traces in this ticket.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Edge ingress adapter emits canonical 'X-Observed-Request' envelope (JSON-compact) when available and falls back to existing header set when not.
2) Node/Go/Python SDK middleware accepts both legacy carriers and 'X-Observed-Request', normalizes to runtime envelope, and attaches 'redwood.trace.fidelity' attribute with values {"none", "partial", "full"}.
3) Trace Resolver library integrates with runtime request path, attaches consistent trace ids for downstream batching metrics and does not increase p99 latency by more than 0.5ms in microbench.
4) End-to-end tracing test (integration harness) shows restored parent-child linkage across edge->gateway->runtime for at least 95% of synthetic requests for which carriers are present.
5) Console dashboard: new 'Trace Fidelity' breakdown and a heatmap showing spike correlation with 5xx errors, validated with sample queries.
6) No regression in unit tests and instrumentation smoke tests; automation added to CI that asserts header normalization for 6 canonical carrier permutations.
design_notes:
Architecture: Introduce an "Observed Request Handshake" at the ingress sidecar: when a request arrives, the sidecar computes a compact provenance envelope (signed HMAC short token + compact JSON payload) containing observed headers, protocol (http/grpc/ws), and a minimal call-path fingerprint. The sidecar sets 'X-Observed-Request' with the compact envelope and leaves legacy headers intact for backward compatibility.

Trace Resolver: A lightweight runtime library (C++ for hot path + thin language bindings) accepts incoming carrier(s) and applies deterministic reconciliation rules in this order: 1) if X-Observed-Request present and HMAC valid => use its canonical trace id and parent id (trust level 'observed_full'); 2) else if OT headers present => canonicalize OT fields (traceparent / tracestate) => trust level 'partial_ot'; 3) else if legacy proprietary headers present => best-effort map => trust level 'partial_legacy'; 4) else create new trace (trust level 'none').

Sampling hints: The envelope carries a fidelity hint (0/1/2) mapping to none/partial/full. The Trace Resolver sets 'redwood.trace.fidelity' tag on the root span and emits an event to the metrics pipeline 'trace.fidelity.<value>' so dashboards can measure fidelity distribution.

Performance: Resolver algorithm implemented with pre-allocated buffers, fast HMAC using our existing crypto kernel, and branchless parsing for the compact envelope. Microbench targets: <0.5ms p99 per request on warm workers.

Backward compatibility: SDK middleware will try X-Observed-Request first, then fall back to existing header parsing. We will add compatibility tests for mixed carriers and mutate only in-flight request context (no persistent changes).

Security: Envelope HMAC prevents clients from forging observed envelopes. Edge-side HMAC key rotated by KMS automated workflow. Envelope includes a tiny TTL (e.g., one minute) to limit replay window.
rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (canary, internal): Deploy ingress sidecar changes to internal staging cluster and opt-in a small percentage (5%) of internal traffic. Enable Trace Resolver in runtime under feature flag 'trace_resolver.canary'. Validate microbench and end-to-end tests.
Phase 2 (external opt-in beta): Release SDK middleware updates (Node/Go/Python) as minor releases, document opt-in steps. Deploy sidecar to customer-facing staging region and invite early-adopters.
Phase 3 (gradual): Flip default for new runtime pools and update console to show Trace Fidelity. Keep fallback paths enabled for 2 weeks post-rollout before starting to deprecate legacy header handling in new pools.
Phase 4 (cleanup): After 90 days, remove debug logging and stale compat code paths behind an internal flag; consider deprecation notices for customers still sending only legacy carriers.
qa_test_plan:
- Unit tests for canonicalization permutations (6 permutations).
- Integration harness that spins up an edge proxy, api-gateway, and runtime with synthetic requests exercising OT/legacy/mixed carriers. Assert parent-child links.
- Load test at 10k rps to validate p99 latency < baseline + 0.5ms.
- Fuzz tests for malformed X-Observed-Request envelopes to ensure graceful rejection and no panics.
- CI gate: new linting rule to ensure any SDK middleware changes add docs and compatibility vectors.
- Dashboard smoke: automated query that checks 'trace.fidelity' metric exists and is emitted during test run.
comments: 2026-02-26 Jordan Kim: Initial spike completed. Prototype HMAC envelope format (base64url compact JSON) in gist. Found that existing crypto kernel supports HMAC-SHA256 with acceptable perf on CPU-accelerated path.

2026-03-02 Leah Chen: Implemented Node middleware and minimal Trace Resolver binding. Microbench shows 0.35ms median, 0.48ms p99 on staging vm (small sample). Need to optimize JSON parsing for Python SDK.

2026-03-04 Priya Nair (Design review): Reviewed envelope schema. Suggest reducing metadata to minimize wire size; prefer integer-coded fidelity (0/1/2) over string to reduce parse cost. Also requested a UI row in console for 'Observed vs Derived' traces.

2026-03-06 Security (Marta Lopez): HMAC approach approved pending KMS key rotation automation. Raised concern about TTL verification across clock skew; recommended allow 5s leeway and add skew metric.
2026-03-08 Josh Park (SRE): Canary plan accepted. Suggested adding fallback counters to measure how often resolver falls back to legacy carriers. Added 'trace.resolver.fallback.count' metric.

2026-03-10 Leah Chen: Updated runtime binding to use branchless parsing and preallocated buffers. Added CI integration test that runs the end-to-end harness nightly. Preparing PRs for edge-proxy and runtime.
